title: Workbook render plan (L5 PLAN)
description: A fully-resolved, cell-level instruction set for rendering one workbook. Every determinism-bearing decision has already been made by the emitter; a conforming renderer contains no business logic and makes no choice of its own. THE CENTRAL RULE: every style record in `styles` is COMPLETE. A renderer never merges a partial style into an existing one, because no partial style is ever expressed. This is what makes the port to openpyxl safe: openpyxl has no partial-style merge, and the plan removes the need for one.

plan_version.description: Bumped only by a human. A renderer MUST refuse a version it does not know rather than render a best guess.

generator.description: Provenance of the plan itself. Never read by the renderer.

default_font.description: The stylesheet's font 0 — the workbook default. N14 asserts the rendered font set is exactly {Carlito}; this is where Carlito is declared.

calc_properties.description: xl/workbook.xml <calcPr>. `iterate` is not cosmetic: the interest <-> debt balance <-> cash sweep circularity is declared and expected (ARCHITECTURE G2), and a workbook opened without iteration on reports it as an error.

comment_author.description: Display name for the single person entry backing every threaded comment (workbook.comments.setSelf).

styles.description: The style table. Each entry is a COMPLETE cell style; cells reference it by index. Index 0 is the default style and must be present.

differential_styles.description: dxf records for conditional formatting. Unlike `styles` these ARE partial by nature — a dxf states only the channels the rule overrides — and that is the OOXML contract, not a merge hazard.

freeze_pane.description: null means no frozen pane. LibreOffice preserves a frozen pane, so this may be written natively; it was patched at package level in the Node emitter only because the legacy workbook library writer dropped it.

outline.description: Sheet-level outline properties. summary_below=false is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a consolidated line sits ABOVE its constituents and Excel puts the collapse control on the wrong side without it.

rows.description: Only rows carrying a non-default property. A row with cells but no height and no outline level need not appear.

cells.description: Address -> cell. A cell may carry a style and nothing else; that is how the sheet's empty-but-styled ground is expressed, and dropping those cells changes the rendered face of the model.

merges.description: Expected empty. `layout.merged_calculation_cells_forbidden` is a standing rule; block titles are centred with horizontal=centerContinuous instead. Present so a renderer can assert the rule rather than silently not implement it.

page_setup.description: LibreOffice does NOT preserve explicit page scaling. If this is populated it must be applied by the terminal patch stage, after the last LibreOffice pass.

defined_names.description: Sheet-scoped defined names. Expected empty for this model.

hidden.description: Nothing on the Operating Model is hidden. Present so the renderer can assert that rather than assume it.

cell.description: A cell states at most one of `f` (formula) and a literal, plus a complete style. `v` alongside `f` is the CACHED result — the value a reader who does not recalculate sees. It is authoritative output of the recalc/patch stages, never something the renderer computes.

s.description: Index into workbook.styles. A complete style, never a patch.

f.description: Formula WITHOUT the leading '='. Modern functions carry the _xlfn. prefix already; a renderer never rewrites formula text.

v.description: Literal value, or the cached result when `f` is present. Dates are serial numbers with a date number format, never date objects.

t.description: Value type. 'n' numeric, 's' string, 'b' boolean, 'e' error, 'd' ISO date. Absent means inferred from `v`.

style.description: A COMPLETE cell style. Every channel the model uses is stated or explicitly absent; a renderer assigns the whole record and never reads the cell's prior state. Two legacy workbook library semantics this design deliberately kills: partial FONT assignment merged (so bold could be added without losing provenance colour), and partial BORDER assignment silently CLEARED the edges it omitted (which is why the Node emitter has a draw-order discipline). Here `border` states the intended edge set outright — omitted edge means no edge, stated edge means that edge — so neither behaviour has to be reproduced.

number_format.description: Excel format code, e.g. '#,##0;(#,##0);"–"'. 'General' for none.

font.description: FONT COLOUR IS THE PROVENANCE LAYER. Input fills were removed, so colour is the whole marking: blue = typed hardcode, black = same-sheet derivation, green = cross-sheet link, white = chrome. Nothing may set it for any other reason, and no renderer may drop it while setting another channel.

color.description: ARGB or RGB hex, upper case. No theme or indexed colours: they resolve against a theme part the renderer must not have to reason about.

fill.description: null means no fill (patternType none). ONE FILL, ONE MEANING: the fill channel belongs to totals and to the uncalculated marker. An input has no fill at all.

border.description: The intended edge set, stated outright. An omitted edge is NO edge.

alignment.description: `centerContinuous` is how the three block titles centre across their blocks without merging. LibreOffice does NOT preserve it, so a pipeline that recalculates must re-apply this at the terminal patch stage.

differential_style.description: A conditional-format override. Partial BY CONTRACT. A dxf may set fill, border, bold/italic and number format. It may NEVER set font colour on a body cell: font colour is the provenance layer and a rule that overrides it silently destroys the one thing the model exists to protect. (The two control-cell toggle rules are the declared exception and are single-cell chrome, not body cells.)

sqref.description: One or more space-separated ranges, OOXML sqref syntax.

formulas.description: Rule formulas WITHOUT a leading '='. Relative/absolute anchoring is significant and is already resolved: `G$185>0` makes each column test its own year.

formula1.description: For type=list this is the quoted comma-joined literal set, e.g. '"Consensus,High,Low"' — exactly as it lands in the XML, so the renderer never has to decide how to quote.

comment.description: A threaded comment. The Node emitter writes these as modern threaded comments (xl/threadedcomments + a person part) with legacy comment shells for compatibility. A renderer that can only write legacy notes must SAY SO rather than silently degrade the channel.
